case_name: Caren Kohl, a.k.a. Caren Rein v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: In her early 50s in 2018; withdrew retirement funds to pay past-due rent and avoid eviction.

adjustments: addition to tax for late filing under section 6651(a)
conceded: Petitioner conceded the distribution was taxable and includible in income
Respondent conceded the section 6651(a) late-filing addition

findings_of_fact.fact: In 2018 petitioner, in her early 50s, received a taxable retirement plan distribution of $10,342
findings_of_fact.snippet: In 2018, when she was in her early 50s , petitioner received a taxable retirement plan distribution of $10,342.

findings_of_fact.fact: Funds withdrawn to pay past-due rent and avoid eviction
findings_of_fact.snippet: She withdrew the money to pay past-due rent and to avoid being evicted by her landlord.

findings_of_fact.fact: Section 72(t)(2)(I) emergency expense exception applies only to distributions after December 31, 2023
findings_of_fact.snippet: However, section 72(t)(2)(I) applies only “ to distributions made after December 31, 2023. ”

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the 10% additional tax under section 72(t) on her 2018 $10,342 retirement plan distribution taken for economic hardship?
issues.holding: Yes; she was under 59 1/2 and no exception applies; the emergency-expense exception of §72(t)(2)(I) applies only to distributions after December 31, 2023
issues.computable_reason: Age under 59 1/2 plus effective-date rule for §72(t)(2)(I) mechanically yields 10% of $10,342

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Section 72(t) 10% additional tax sustained on $10,342 distribution; late-filing addition conceded by respondent

notes: Deficiency amount not stated in opinion. Court notes §§7491(c) and 6751(b) do not apply to §72(t). Derived: 10% x $10,342 = $1,034.20 (not stated by court). Snippets F1/F3 preserve PDF spacing artifacts.
